title: Machine-readable merge readiness and delivery-slice relationships
objective: Extend the ticket engine so independently integrable work slices can carry an auditable, harness-neutral merge-readiness state while larger objectives remain open and are split into linked follow-on tickets. Keep ticket lifecycle status separate, and expose identical semantics through the canonical schema, engine, CLI, MCP, validation, and query views.

acceptance_criteria.text: Ticket lifecycle status remains draft/active/resolved/archived; merge or integration readiness is represented as an independent machine-readable dimension, not by overloading status or ad-hoc labels.
A broad objective can be split into independently deliverable tickets while preserving explicit parent/child or split/follow-on relationships, the remaining scope, and audit history.
A readiness claim is explicit and auditable with the relevant commit/ref and verification evidence; the engine does not infer readiness from prose, branch names, or harness identity.
Canonical JSON schema, engine validation/persistence, and backward-compatible migration/default behavior agree on the new representation.
CLI and MCP expose equivalent create/read/update/query behavior and reject the same invalid readiness and relationship transitions.
Tests cover lifecycle/readiness independence, split relationships, evidence requirements, old-ticket compatibility, and CLI/MCP parity; documentation gives a harness-neutral workflow.

needed: Schema and migration tests for old tickets with no readiness metadata
Engine tests for readiness state transitions/evidence and split/follow-on relationships
CLI and MCP parity tests for create/get/update/search/validation
Board/list/search tests for presenting readiness without conflating it with lifecycle status
Confirm the canonical representation can express an independently merge-ready child while its parent/follow-on scope remains active, using the same operations through CLI and MCP.
Review all ticket relationship operations in the current CLI/MCP schemas; close parity gaps rather than adding a second workflow model.
